questions.specialNote: C is the Made Easy reference answer. As written, A is also needed for a module containing compiled code, and B is needed when address fixups are required.
questions.reason: The linker uses C to resolve references from other modules. It also needs the compiled code (A) and any necessary relocation records (B). The linker can assign absolute addresses for internal symbols during linking.
questions.note: The 1995 paper scan and GATE Overflow read “What information need not be included in an object module?” Made Easy and the app omit the negation. GATE Overflow lists C for the negative stem. With the usual relocatable-object assumptions, the technical answer to the original negative stem is D. To keep C as a unique answer, ask “Which information lets the linker resolve references from other modules to symbols defined in this module?”

questions.reason: The kernel delivers SIGINT by arranging for the process to enter its registered handler on return to user mode. The process's handler therefore executes in user mode.
questions.note: Both printed keys select kernel mode (GATE Overflow B maps to app A by option text). The GATE IT 2005 paper and the app ask about the handler registered by the process. The Linux signal(7) manual confirms that the handler executes after the transition to user mode.

sources.answer: D (user mode, verified by the signal delivery documentation)

questions.specialNote: With POSIX ln, both commands fail because the destinations already exist. All three files keep their contents.
questions.reason: POSIX ln -s requires -f to remove an existing destination. Both destinations are existing regular files. Both commands reported File exists in the command trace, and all three contents were preserved.
questions.note: Made Easy's B assumes the destinations are overwritten. The original paper also uses ln -s, and POSIX documents some historical variants of ln with different overwrite behavior. Specify POSIX ln and add “None of I, II or III.” To retain B instead, use ln -sf in both commands and stipulate permission to replace entries in the directory.

questions.reason: If /etc/passwd is the only matching pathname, find lists ./passwd, and ls passwd identifies that same file. The other choices read or search the file contents.
questions.note: The GATE IT 2005 paper matches the app's intended command. Made Easy prints password and omits the starting path, although its key selects ls passwd. For the intended A, specify that /etc/passwd is the only matching pathname under /etc and ask which command identifies the same file. find is recursive and its output includes the ./ prefix.

questions.reason: The positive total weight is constant across schedules. Ordering adjacent jobs i then j instead of j then i changes the weighted sum by w_j t_i − w_i t_j. The first order is no worse when w_i/t_i ≥ w_j/t_j, so sorting by descending ratio is optimal.
